title: Siting a new packaging line: three sources
bodyMd:
**Source 1 — Memo from the Operations Director, 14 March**

We must choose between the Halvern site and the Kestrel Park site for the new packaging line. Halvern is a brownfield plot we already own; Kestrel Park would be leased. Either site can house the line. Halvern needs its floor slab replaced before any equipment can be installed, and our engineers put that work at 11 weeks; Kestrel Park is ready for fit-out immediately. Fit-out itself takes 9 weeks at either site, and cannot overlap the slab work. The line must be producing by 1 December.

**Source 2 — Email from Finance, 17 March**

On cost: owning Halvern saves us the lease, but the slab replacement is capital spending of £1,400,000 that we would not incur at Kestrel Park. The Kestrel Park lease is £310,000 a year on a five-year term with no break clause. Over five years the lease therefore costs more than the slab, which is why I recommend Halvern. I have not included the cost of running the line, because our analysis assumes it is identical at the two sites — an assumption Operations has not yet confirmed.

**Source 3 — Site data**

See the accompanying table of site data.

data.caption: Source 3: site data for the two candidate locations.

accessibilityText: Three sources about choosing a site for a new packaging line. Source 1, an operations memo dated 14 March, says the choice is between Halvern, which the company owns but whose floor slab needs 11 weeks of replacement work first, and Kestrel Park, which would be leased and is ready for fit-out immediately; fit-out takes 9 weeks at either site and cannot overlap the slab work, and the line must be producing by 1 December. Source 2, a finance email dated 17 March, says the slab costs 1,400,000 pounds of capital spending, the Kestrel Park lease is 310,000 pounds a year for five years with no break clause, that the lease therefore costs more than the slab over five years, and that running costs were assumed identical at both sites although operations has not confirmed this. Source 3 is a two-row table: Halvern is 62 kilometres from the distribution hub, has 4,800 square metres of floor area, 2,900 workers within 20 kilometres, and work can begin on 1 April; Kestrel Park is 18 kilometres from the hub, has 4,100 square metres, 7,400 workers within 20 kilometres, and work can begin on 1 May.

provenance.notes: Original multi-source set written for this question bank. Sites, companies, dates and figures are invented; nothing is drawn from any published Multi-Source Reasoning item.
